content: Ibn Turka argues the written form intermixes with perception to the point of total identification because letterforms reach the light of vision by light, and separate rays of light unite rather than merely meet, so two clashing colours can be seen at once without either being denatured, unlike sounds carried by air. Written letterforms are thus not bodies and cannot clash, and stand unique among sensory objects in their abstraction from material constraints; the more descended such forms are, the more perfect and comprehensive.
